# Planning's approval page, `artifacts/plan.html`, is generated by `await-approval` from the markdown, never written by an agent

## Context and Problem Statement

A reviewer of a UI plan had to open every frame and spec rule by hand. One page showing the plan, each phase, its frames and cited spec sections helps only if it is never older than the markdown a coder builds from.

## Considered Options

- Approve `plan.html`; `await-approval` rebuilds it from `plan.md`, the phase files and `design/` whenever its `--file` is `artifacts/plan.html`
- Keep approving `plan.md`; `await-approval` also writes `plan.html` beside it
- Approve `plan.html`, built only when the skill passes a `--build` flag to `await-approval`

## Decision Outcome

Chosen: approve `plan.html`, rebuilt by `await-approval`, because every request for approval, including each one after a reviewer's revision, passes through that one call, so the page cannot be stale and no skill can forget a flag. Approving `plan.md` instead would put the Approve button on a file the reviewer is not reading, with the page opened separately. A build error fails the call and records no request. Implement still consumes the markdown `plan` artifact; planning registers both `plan` and `plan-page`.

## Consequences

A page edited by hand is overwritten at the next approval request. `await-approval` now reads the plan files, not only the file it is given.
